sections.heading: C — Highways, Interchanges, Roundabouts
sections.markdown:
## C — Highways, Interchanges, Roundabouts

FACT_ID: sec15-F01 | anchor: A01
This chapter ports basics into live scenarios from odd roads to weather and emergencies [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-F02 | anchor: A01
Intersections span every merge or crossing: cross streets, side streets, drives, lots, and public roads [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-F03 | anchor: A01
Work crossings in three looks: read type and controls ahead, scan for a clear path, then sweep left-right-left for cars and walkers while assuming no gifts of space [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-F04 | anchor: A01
Distrust strangers' blinkers, since they may overshoot your turn or stick on, especially unsticking motorcycle lamps; move only once they truly swing [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-F05 | anchor: A02
Split rural four-lane crossings at the median: halt at the sign, take the median on a left-side gap, wait there, then finish on a right-side gap [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec15-F06 | anchor: A02
Such roads run fast and demand focus, and long rigs may overhang skinny medians [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec15-F07 | anchor: A02
On-ramps run entrance scan, acceleration and merge at traffic speed without stopping short of need, then joined travel where incumbents slide to admit you [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec15-F08 | anchor: A03
Reduced-conflict crossings turn side-road lefts into rights, then left-lane merges and U-turns at median gaps, facing one direction at a time with no two-way gap wait [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F09 | anchor: A04
Diverging diamonds briefly drive the wrong side to unsnarl two busy roads with shorter signal waits [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec15-F10 | anchor: A05
Roundabouts circle counterclockwise signalless around islands under yield guidance at calming speeds [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec15-F11 | anchor: A05
Single-lane drivers approach at advisory pace yielding to crosswalk users, then yield at the line to circle traffic and join gaps counterclockwise [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec15-F12 | anchor: A05
Ride through without stopping, then signal and peel right, again yielding to crosswalk users [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec15-F13 | anchor: A05
Walkers look left, cross to the splitter island, look right, and finish across [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec15-F14 | anchor: A05
Cyclists generally walk bikes as pedestrians, though veterans may ride motorist-style mid-lane off the curb while yielding to crosswalks [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec15-F15 | anchor: A05
Multi-lane rings demand pre-picked lanes per signs, full yield on entry, right signals past the pre-exit street, and cross-lane awareness [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec15-F16 | anchor: A05
Inside rings forbid lane swaps, truck shadowing against straddles and blind eyes, and overrunning the outside lane past its limit [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec15-F17 | anchor: A05
Never stroll circulating lanes to the island, and cede aprons to long trailers' rear wheels [A05].
Why it matters: the island ban and apron purpose are the two most-missed roundabout details.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec15-F18 | anchor: A06
Loose gravel steals grip, so slow down, shun sharp wheel, ease pedals, and stretch gaps [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-F19 | anchor: A06
Trees, corn, buildings, hills, and dust blind rural sightlines, so map blind spots early [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-F20 | anchor: A06
Unsigned gravel crossings want caution, low speed, and stop readiness with no faith in dust clouds; left-side cars yield and nobody assumes anything [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-F21 | anchor: A06
Soft rural shoulders suck cars ditchward, so creep near shoulders and past oncoming wheels [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-F22 | anchor: A06
Burn low beams through heavy dust to be seen [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0055]

Misconceptions: roundabouts need stops like four-ways, yet yields rule them; median waiting is forbidden, yet two-stage crossings demand it; dust clouds reliably betray cross traffic, yet they cannot be trusted.

Mnemonic: left right left, yield the ring, cross in halves, gravel gentle.

Glossary: reduced-conflict intersection (a right-then-U-turn crossing design); diverging diamond (an interchange briefly swapping road sides); splitter island (a raised pedestrian refuge in crossings); truck apron (a paved ring fitting long-vehicle wheels).

Dynamic facts: none in these pages; every intersection, interchange, roundabout, and gravel rule above is stable handbook knowledge with no date-variable or place-variable values.
